post.title: Every Stock Market Term Explained in 13 Minutes
post.content:
Milo's friend Benny talks about going long on a blue chip, getting shaken out and catching a short squeeze. Milo nods along and understands none of it. So he spends one year in Marketland with Lexi, a tiny pocket dictionary, and learns the whole language of the stock market, month by month.

In this animated explainer you'll learn about 75 stock market terms in plain English: stocks, shares, IPOs and tickers; brokers, assets and liabilities; bid, ask and the spread; market, limit and stop-loss orders; volume and liquidity; bull and bear markets and volatility; market cap, blue chips and penny stocks; balance sheets, EPS, the P/E ratio, book value, dividends, yield and ROI; portfolios, bonds, commodities, index funds, ETFs, mutual funds, hedge funds and IRAs; unicorns, whales, bubbles, panic selling, circuit breakers, black swans and dead cat bounces; going long, short selling, short squeezes, leverage, options and futures; pump and dumps and insider trading; day trading, swing trading, technical vs fundamental analysis and averaging down; and the two boring superpowers, dollar cost averaging and compound interest.

⏱️ CHAPTERS
0:00 Welcome to Marketland
0:46 January: Owning a Slice
1:48 February: The Order Window
2:48 March: Market Weather
3:43 April: Reading the Label
5:02 June: Baskets
6:13 July: The Zoo
6:44 August: The Storm
7:31 September: The Dangerous Toolbox
8:39 October: Watch Your Pockets
9:05 November: How People Play
10:04 December: The Boring Superpowers
11:00 Your Wallet

💬 Which term did you pretend to understand before today? Tell us in the comments.
🔔 Subscribe to Finance with Stromi for money, explained simply.

Milo, Lexi, Benny, Marge, Bruno, Ursula, Gus, Pip, Dot and Ploppy Pancake Co. are made-up. Every worked number is a made-up example. This video is general education, not personal financial advice. Figures and rules are as of November 2026 and change over time. Investing involves risk, including loss of money; leverage, short selling, options and futures can lose more than you put in.

Sources: IRS Notice 2025-67 (2026 IRA limit $7,500); NYSE Rule 7.12 and Nasdaq market-wide circuit breakers (7% / 13% / 20%); SEC Exchange Act Rule 3a51-1 (penny stocks) and Rule 10b-5 (insider trading); SEC investor alerts on pump-and-dump schemes; Aileen Lee, TechCrunch (2013, "unicorn"); Nassim Nicholas Taleb, "The Black Swan" (2007); Eugene Fama and the efficient market hypothesis (Nobel 2013); GameStop price history Dec 2020 to Jan 2021; Barber, Lee, Liu & Odean (2014) and Chague, De-Losso & Giovannetti (2019) on day-trader results. Compound interest and inflation examples computed for this video (7% a year and 3% inflation are assumptions, never guaranteed).

Music by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Tracks: Hep Cats, Investigations, Sneaky Snitch, Monkeys Spinning Monkeys, Easy Lemon, Pixel Peeker Polka - faster, Fluffing a Duck, Bumbly March, Thinking Music, Carefree, Hidden Agenda, Dark Times, Wallpaper, Gymnopedie No 1.
